The allegation dates back to 2023, when a joint security check involving the National Intelligence Service (NIS) and the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) found the NEC had exaggerated the results of its own security inspection amid concerns over the vulnerability of its computer servers to cyberattacks. The NEC had reported a perfect score of 100 the previous year, but a reassessment by the NIS and KISA produced a score of only 31.5. items.summary: Seoul will spend 19.2 billion won ($14.2 million) through 2031 to restore forests on Mount Nam and build new attractions there, including a 360-degree observatory at the summit, the city government said Thursday. Located in central Seoul, Mount Nam is one of the capital city’s best-known landmarks. The city formally announced an urban regeneration plan for Mount Nam and nearby areas, including the Myeong-dong shopping district and Yejang Park, on Thursday. The plan covers about 3.11 million square meters and has 15 projects in four areas. Eight of them are early-stage projects meant to spur further development with the allotted funding. A key part of the plan is a gondola that will run about 832 meters from Yejang Park, near Myeongdong Station, to the summit. It is designed to carry more than 1,600 passengers an hour, over three times as many as the existing cable car. The city said the gondola will make the summit easier to reach for wheelchair users and others with limited mobility. Its operating profits will go toward restoring the mountain’s ecosystem. The joint team from Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) and Samsung Research built a prototype featuring a 1.5-millimeter-thick waveguide—the transparent channel that guides light from a tiny projector into the wearer’s eye—using engineered nanostructures called metasurfaces. The findings were published Thursday in the journal Nature, according to the Ministry of Science and ICT. For years, technology giants from Meta and Apple to Google and Samsung have raced to build lightweight smart glasses capable of overlaying turn-by-turn directions, translations and messages onto the real world. In a survey of 1,001 adults nationwide conducted Monday through Wednesday, positive assessments of Lee's job performance fell 2 percentage points to 44 percent from two weeks earlier, according to the National Barometer Survey (NBS). Negative assessments rose 3 percentage points to 47 percent. Lee's disapproval rating had remained higher than his approval rating for several weeks before the trend reversed in the previous poll. The survey also showed that 51 percent of respondents said Lee should scale back his use of social media to directly communicate with the public on his policy direction, citing concerns that remarks made "without sufficient deliberation" could cause confusion. Another 42 percent supported his use of social media for communication. Jamal expressed deep gratitude to the Korean government and people for their continued support, urging them "to continue to build solidarity with the world." items.summary: A police complaint was filed Thursday accusing ruling party Rep. Choi Min-hee of defamation for referring to journalists as "a pack of hyenas." The complaint against Choi of the Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) was filed with the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency a week after the lawmaker made the comment in a KakaoTalk group chat while referring to an image of photo and video journalists covering a general meeting of DPK lawmakers. She also described the journalists as "doing everything to take videos that sow discord." The complainant, Lee Jong-bae, a former Seoul city councilmember affiliated with the main opposition People Power Party, said Choi's comments revealed her perception of the press and exposed a double standard that chants democracy but scorns journalists that cause discomfort. Choi held a press conference at the National Assembly on Wednesday and apologized for her remarks.

Participants explored strategic responses to the rapidly changing international order and discussed ways to deepen Korea-ASEAN ties. items.title: Saudi Arabia secures top global rankings in IMD’s 2026 AI Index
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯在IMD 2026年人工智能指数中位居全球前列
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia has achieved leading global positions in several artificial intelligence (AI) indicators in the IMD World Digital and AI Ranking 2026, released on Wednesday by the International Institute for Management Development (IMD), which assesses 70 countries. Saudi Arabia ranked second globally in companies’ awareness of AI-related cybersecurity risks and protection of sensitive data in corporate AI systems. It placed fourth globally in three indicators: implementation of the national AI strategy, corporate adoption of AI, and public access to AI technologies. Saudi Arabia ranked fifth globally in AI adoption and in three sub-indicators: public trust in AI, regulatory frameworks for AI-related issues, and corporate investment in AI. It ranked seventh globally in AI skills, cities’ use of AI to improve service quality, and companies’ efforts to address bias in AI algorithms. It also placed eighth in AI readiness, ninth in private-sector AI investment, and 11th in AI and capital investment. The results reflect Saudi Arabia’s progress in developing its data and AI ecosystem, strengthening readiness, and expanding AI adoption across sectors. They also highlight efforts to develop national capabilities, stimulate investment, and improve regulatory frameworks, enhancing globalcompetitiveness and supporting Saudi Vision 2030 objectives.

items.title: Minister Al-Rabiah: Hajj Conference participation surges fivefold
items.title_zh: 拉比阿部长：参加朝觐会议的人数激增五倍
items.summary: JEDDAH — Minister of Hajj and Umrah Tawfiq Al-Rabiah said the sixth Hajj Conference and Exhibition has seen significant growth in participation and international interest. The number of participating entities has risen from 84 in 2022 to approximately 520 in the current edition, representing growth of more than fivefold. Al-Rabiah said attendance is expected to exceed 200,000 visitors by the end of the event, with participation from more than 150 countries, including leaders, ministers, and muftis from around the world. He said these figures reflect the conference’s growth, rising international interest, and strong engagement, along with contracts and partnerships aimed at improving pilgrim services and advancing the Hajj ecosystem. The minister thanked the Saudi leadership for its patronage and support, describing this support as a cornerstone of continued improvements in services for pilgrims.

items.title: Saudi interior minister: Houthi militia’s terrorist acts undermine regional security
items.title_zh: 沙特内政部长：胡塞武装的恐怖主义行为破坏了地区安全
items.summary: MANAMA — Interior ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states held their 43rd meeting in Manama, Bahrain on Wednesday. The meeting was chaired by Minister of Interior of Bahrain and current session chair Gen. Sheikh Rashid bin Abdullah Al Khalifa.Addressing the session, Saudi Minister of Interior Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud bin Naif stressed that the security of GCC states is indivisible and that any threat against one member state constitutes a direct threat to the entire Gulf security system.“The terrorist Houthi militia’s targeting of civilians and civilian and economic infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, as well as its blatant attacks on the Two Holy Mosques, are acts that cannot be justified under any pretext or in any form,” he said while emphasizing that these actions threaten civilian lives andundermine security and stability in Yemen and the wider region. Prince Abdulaziz highlighted the exceptional circumstances and highly sensitive regional and international developments, which pose challenges requiring a shift from merely responding to security events to anticipating them and preparing in advance to address them.This will be through comprehensive implementation plans and intensified efforts to coordinate and strengthen joint action in confronting regional and international challenges. Prince Abdulaziz welcomed the GCC interior ministers to their second home, Saudi Arabia, which will host the 44th session of the meeting. He expressed Saudi Arabia’s eagerness to continue and strengthen joint Gulf security efforts. The meeting and the decisions it adopts reflect a genuine commitment, dedicated efforts and a unified position, in a manner that fulfills the aspirations of GCC leaders to protect their countries and communities and strengthen their security and stability. The GCC ministers of interior discussed the items on the agenda, which aim to strengthen joint security cooperation among the member states.

items.title: King Salman and Crown Prince offer condolences to Niger’s president on his father’s death
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王和王储对尼日尔总统的父亲去世表示哀悼
items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman offered condolences to President of Niger and Head of State Gen. Abdourahamane Tiani on the death of his father Elhadj Tiani Hassane.In separate cables sent to Tiani, the King and the Crown Prince expressed their deepest condolences and sincere sympathy to the president and the deceased’s family. They prayed to God Almighty to grant the deceased His mercy and forgiveness, and accommodate him in His Paradise.

items.title: King Salman and Crown Prince congratulate Alliana on taking oath as Paraguay president
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王和王储祝贺阿利亚娜宣誓就任巴拉圭总统
items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman congratulated Pedro Alliana on taking the constitutional oath as president of Paraguay.In cables sent to Alliana, the King and the Crown Prince expressed their sincere congratulations and best wishes for the president's success and for further progress and prosperity for the people of Paraguay. Pedro Alliana has been sworn in as the new president of Paraguay, after a banking scandal led to the impeachment of his predecessor, Santiago Pena. On Friday, Alliana, 52, took the oath of office to become the South American country’s 53rd president. Previously, Alliana had served as vice president under Pena since the start of the latter’s term in 2023.

items.title: Bahrain’s king, crown prince review Gulf security cooperation with GCC interior ministers
items.title_zh: 巴林国王和王储与海合会内政部长讨论海湾安全合作
items.summary: MANAMA — King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa of Bahrain received at Al-Sakhir Palace here on Wednesday Saudi Minister of Interior Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud bin Naif and other interior ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states, ahead of their meeting held in Manama. During the meeting, Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud conveyed the greetings of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman to the king of Bahrain, along with their wishes for continued progress and prosperity for Bahrain and its people. The king of Bahrain and the ministers reviewed the progress of joint Gulf security cooperation and efforts to strengthen coordination and integration among GCC member states in security fields. The king wished the interior ministers success in their meeting, expressing hope that it would help enhance security and stability across GCC member states. Also on Wednesday, Crown Prince, Deputy Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces and Prime Minister of Bahrain Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa received interior ministers of the GCC states. During the meeting, Prince Abdulaziz bin Saud conveyed the greetings of Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman to Prince Salman bin Hamad, along with his wishes for continued progress and prosperity for Bahrain and its people. Prince Salman bin Hamad commended the efforts of the interior ministers during their meeting and the outcomes achieved in strengthening the security and stability of GCC member states. Prince Salman and the interior ministers reviewed the security cooperation among GCC countries and the ongoing efforts to enhance coordination and integration in security-related fields.

items.title: 5 Houthi missiles, 2 UAVs targeting Riyadh, Makkah, and other regions intercepted
items.title_zh: 5枚胡塞导弹、2架无人机袭击利雅得、麦加和其他地区，均被拦截
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed three cruise missiles, fired by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Riyadh region. This was revealed by Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen. The air defenses also intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles, launched by the Houthi militia, in the western region," he said. Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki also stated that two UAVs launched by the Houthi militia were intercepted and destroyed in the Makkah and the southern regions.

items.title: King Salman and Crown Prince offer condolences to Turkish president over deadly steel plant blast
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王和王储就钢铁厂爆炸事故向土耳其总统表示哀悼
items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman offered condolences to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan over the death of several people in a steel plant explosion in Izmir Province. In separate cables sent to Erdoğan, the King and the Crown Prince expressed their deepest condolences and sincere sympathy to the president, the families of the deceased, and the Turkish people. They prayed to God Almighty to grant the deceased His mercy and forgiveness, give their families patience and solace, and grant the injured a speedy recovery. At least 18 people were killed and 12 others injured in an explosion at an iron and steel factory near the port city of Izmir in western Turkey on Monday. All those killed and injured were workers at the Habas Demir Celik plant in Aliaga, one of the country's leading steel producers, authorities said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia among world’s top 3 in AI talent growth and model development
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯在人工智能人才增长和模型开发方面跻身全球前三名
items.summary: RIYADH — The Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA) released a comprehensive study on the state of artificial intelligence in the Kingdom, reviewing national progress across seven main pillars and 15 sub-pillars spanning regulatory frameworks, investments, digital infrastructure, data governance, human capital, research and innovation, and institutional adoption. The report details Saudi Arabia’s advanced positions across international benchmarks, including ranking third globally in AI talent growth rate under the 2026 Stanford HAI Index, third globally and first regionally in the development of leading AI models under the 2025 index, and fifth globally in AI sector growth according to the 2025 Observer Index. The Kingdom also secured 26 awards at the 2025 World Artificial Intelligence Competition for Youth and officially joined the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence in 2026. In digital infrastructure, domestic data center capacity expanded by 115.8 percent between 2023 and 2025. National compute power is anchored by the Shaheen III supercomputer—leading the GCC on the 2026 TOP500 list—alongside the Hexagon Data Center, the world' largest government-owned Tier IV facility with a 480-megawatt capacity. Saudi Arabia also hosts nine hyperscale cloud regions by mid-2026, including four currently under development by global providers. Regarding national data ecosystems, some 515 government systems have been integrated into the National Data Lake under the National Data Bank, aggregating 5.87 petabytes from over 90 government entities in 2026. Open datasets exceeded 21,800 across 346 public and private contributors during the same year. Furthermore, over 500 billion Arabic data units powered the development of the "ALLaM 34B" large language model in 2025, while the King Salman Global Academy for Arabic Language's "Falak" platform reached 2.2 billion words. On human capital, the study found that 84 percent of the Saudi public is familiar with AI concepts, with more than 1.2 million beneficiaries participating in the first phase of the "SAMAI" initiative by July 2026. From 2021 to 2025, over 69,300 technical graduates entered the market, contributing to a 15 percent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in domestic AI talent density. In research and innovation, AI-focused scientific publications registered a 37.4 percent CAGR between 2021 and 2025, while related patent filings grew by 34.52 percent from 2020 to 2024. Local development produced eight large language models and 58 specialized AI applications, according to the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology's 2026 report. Government adoption reached high maturity, with 90 percent of public entities maintaining an AI strategy, 97 percent deploying or building AI tools, 77 percent enforcing formal AI governance, and 63 percent complying with SDAIA's national principles. Nearly half (48 percent) of adopting entities reported internal operational efficiency gains exceeding 10 percent. The study also affirmed the Kingdom's global leadership across key sub-indices, ranking first worldwide in women's empowerment in AI, first in AI security, privacy, and encryption, first in digital readiness, third in student adoption of generative AI, sixth in government strategy, and seventh in financial sector funding.

items.title: Makkah deputy emir reviews Hajj ministry’s efforts in serving pilgrims
items.title_zh: 麦加副埃米尔审查朝觐事务部为朝觐者提供服务的举措
items.summary: JEDDAH — Deputy Emir of Makkah Prince Saud bin Mishaal received Minister of Hajj and Umrah Tawfiq Al-Rabiah at the emirate headquarters in Jeddah on Wednesday. During the meeting, Al-Rabiah briefed the deputy emir on the ministry’s efforts in the current Umrah season, as well as the digital service ecosystem designed to facilitate visits to the Grand Mosque, and initiatives to develop logistical services and infrastructure, all aimed at enhancing the quality of services provided to pilgrims. They also reviewed key aspects of the sixth Hajj Conference and Exhibition, which focuses on advancing the Hajj and Umrah service ecosystem and continuously improving the pilgrim experience.
